title: Chandas Shastra & Binary Mathematics
price: HTML · 1 chapter · not the classical manuscript

chapters.overview: Pingala (c. 3rd century BCE) developed a binary number system (Laghu/Guru) to compute all possible poetic meters. His algorithms (Prastara, Nashta, Uddishta) represent early combinatorics, Pascal's Triangle (Meru), and Fibonacci numbers.

slokas.deva:
द्विरर्धे ।
रूपे शून्यम् ।
द्विः शून्ये ।
तावदर्धे तद्गुणितम् ॥
slokas.translit:
dvir ardhe |
rūpe śūnyam |
dviḥ śūnye |
tāvad ardhe tadguṇitam ||

anvaya.en: When (the count) can be halved: halve it and write two (dvi)
When one (rūpa) has to be subtracted (odd count): write zero (śūnya)
Reading the marks back: at a zero, double
At a "half" mark, multiply by itself (square)

slokas.translation: If the count is halvable, halve it and write "two"; if not, subtract one and write "zero". Reading the marks back, double at a zero and square at a two — Piṅgala's fast-exponentiation for 2ⁿ. The halve/subtract sequence is the binary expansion of n, which the snippet reproduces (modern reading: 0 ↔ halved, 1 ↔ one subtracted).
slokas.source: स्रोत अपरीक्षित · source unverified — editions/pingala-full-edition.html (१.२) carries «द्विरर्धे । रूपे शून्यम् ।»; the sūtras «द्विः शून्ये» and «तावदर्धे तद्गुणितम्» and the numbering 8.28–31 have no witness in this repository.
